## **Gaps — no SOP yet**

- **Member Onboarding** – first 7 days experience (induction booking, fitness assessment, class intro protocol, buddy assignment, digital systems access). No documented funnel = inconsistent first impressions & higher early churn.
- **Cancellation & Churn** – no trigger-based win-back sequence or pause-to-reactivation path. Members leave silently; no systematic recovery attempt.
- **Member Pause** – unclear pause eligibility, comms, hold duration, reactivation checks. Gaps here bleed into retention metrics.
- **Member Data Privacy & GDPR** – no documented consent capture, data retention, subject access request, or breach protocol. Legal/compliance risk.
- **Class Quality Audit Checklist** – no standardised observation tool for coaching standards, safety, energy, pacing. Can't measure if coaching SOP is actually being delivered.
- **Complaints & Incident Logging** – no SOP for handling member complaints, near-misses, injuries, safeguarding flags. Exposure if pattern goes undetected.
- **Health & Safety Monthly Review** – no documented process to review accidents, hazards, equipment checks, compliance. Reactive vs. proactive.

- **Weekly Key Coach Tasks** – vague; needs specifics on session prep, member notes review, performance feedback cycles, class setup checklist.

# Service Menu Build — The Forge

**Stop overthinking this. You need two documents done in parallel, not sequential.**

• **Coach version first (2-3 hours max):** List every offering with internal cost, margin targets, and who delivers it. This is your profitability dashboard — coaches need to know what pays them. Include: class types, PT rates (hourly + package discounts), specialized programs (strength, nutrition coaching), retail/supplements. Make it brutally honest about what's actually profitable for The Forge.

• **Member version is a sales tool, not a copy of the coach version:** Highlight benefits and outcomes, not just features. "6-week strength foundation program £180" beats "12 sessions £15/session." Group offerings by *member goal* (strength, confidence, community) not by service type. Pricing should feel like value, not a menu.

• **Kill the "what's included" ambiguity NOW:** Specify exactly — locker access? Showers? Guest passes? Nutrition guides? This prevents refund/complaint friction. One sentence per perk. If it's unclear in your head, it's costing you retention.

• **Test pricing on 5-10 existing members this week:** Not a focus group chat. Real convo: "We're clarifying our packages. Does this feel right for what you get?" You'll catch pricing blind spots before launch.

• **Format matters more than you think:** Use a simple one-pager PDF for members (shareable, Instagram-storable). Coaches get a spreadsheet they can actually reference during consultations.

**Timeline: Draft by end of week. Live by week's end.**

# THE FORGE — FRACTIONAL CFO PRIORITIES

## REVENUE — URGENT: Member Value is Collapsing

• **Rev/member has crashed from £145 (July) to £106 (October)**. You're adding members (167 vs 136 in July) but earning 27% less per head. This is the single biggest profit leak. Audit what changed: Are new members on lower-tier plans? Have card/class fees dropped? Have you stopped upselling PT, nutrition plans, or apparel? Close this gap to £130+/member immediately — that alone recovers £4k/month on your current base.

• **Churn spiked to 12.8% in May** then stabilised around 5–6% since June — good. But your revenue didn't recover proportionally. Focus retention ops on the first 90 days (where most drop) via onboarding touchpoints, intro PT sessions, and community integration; quantify churn by cohort (new vs legacy members) to spot where the leak is.

• **September revenue peaked at £22k** on 159 members (your highest). You then *lost* 8 members by October but revenue fell £4.2k (19%). The drop wasn't member count—it was value per member. Run a pricing audit: are October joiners on intro offers that haven't expired? If so, systematize a *retention price* (lower tier to stick) vs *acquisition price*, then auto-graduate or upsell at 6 months.

## EXPENSES — Check Payroll & Occupancy Post-Relocation

• **Post-relocation (May onwards) you're running 159–167 members on a larger space.** Revenue trend is flat/choppy (£15.7k–£22k range) despite headcount growth. Stress-test the new studio's break-even: what's your monthly fixed cost (rent, rates, utilities, insurance, base staff)? If it's >£8k–£10k and membership revenue isn't growing proportionally, you're underwater on the expansion. Model: Can you reach 200 members on current pricing to fully absorb the facility cost, or do you need to *increase occupancy rate* (classes/PT) on existing members to offset?
